exposure: Parents' perceived and actual knowledge about adolescent health guidelines
Parent and adolescent engagement in health behaviors (physical activity, dietary intake, sleep, screen time, substance use)
Barriers and facilitators to engaging in healthy behaviors
Delivery and component preferences for a parent-based preventive intervention
outcome: Parental knowledge levels regarding adolescent health guidelines
Rates of adolescent adherence to national health recommendations for physical activity, vegetable intake, and screen time
Key parental concerns about adolescent health behaviors (e.g., technology use, mental health, e-cigarette use)
Preferred delivery methods and components for future parent-based preventive interventions
cohort: 179 parents of children aged 11 to 18 years residing in Australia completed an anonymous web-based survey.
finding: Parents demonstrated moderate perceived but low actual knowledge of adolescent health guidelines, and preferred brief, web-based interventions focused on increasing knowledge, skill-building for goal-setting, and incorporating behavior change techniques.
